Summary:
The blog-post is a 2017 year-in-review by Viktoriya Krakovna that briefly describes several AI-safety research outputs (reward-corruption, AI-Safety Gridworlds, interpretability work), community-building activities (Beneficial-AI conference, AI-Safety Open Discussion group) and personal self-tracking projects.  Only sections that present explicit AI-safety problems, reasoning, and interventions were extracted.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[88]  
• The post explicitly links each intervention to a clearly stated problem, allowing medium-to-strong edge confidence.  
• All nodes are connected through the shared “inadequate research infrastructure for AI safety” barrier node; no satellites or direct risk→intervention edges remain.  
• Instruction set could improve by adding an explicit “barrier” edge type and by clarifying whether paths must preserve strict causal semantics or may use looser “motivational” links when directionality would otherwise invert.

Inference strategy justification:  
Where the source only cites the title of a paper or event, moderate inference was used to reconstruct the specific problem addressed and the concrete intervention (e.g. interpreting the reward-corruption paper as proposing corruption-resistant RL algorithms).  All such edges are marked confidence 2–3.

Extraction completeness explanation:  
All distinct research contributions and community actions that the post claims mitigate an AI-safety problem were captured, yielding 18 interconnected nodes—adequate for a ~1 k-word source.

Key limitations:  
• The post is a high-level summary; fine-grained methodological details had to be inferred.  
• Personal health experiments were ignored because they do not feed into AI-safety risk pathways.
